Brahmajālasuttaṃ

Dīgha Nikāya 1
← Back to Dīgha Nikāya
1
1. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca nāḷandaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Suppiyopi kho paribbājako antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca nāḷandaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti saddhiṃ antevāsinā brahmadattena māṇavena. Tatra sudaṃ suppiyo paribbājako anekapariyāyena buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; suppiyassa pana paribbājakassa antevāsī brahmadatto māṇavo anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Itiha te ubho ācariyantevāsī aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā anubaddhā (ka. sī. pī.) honti bhikkhusaṅghañca.
1. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was traveling along the main road between Rājagṛha and Nālandā with a large company of monks (bhikkhusaṅgha), with about five hundred monks.

Suppiya the wanderer (paribbājaka) was also traveling along the road between Rājagṛha and Nālandā, together with his pupil, the youth Brahmadatta.

There, it is said, Suppiya the wanderer spoke in many ways in dispraise of the Buddha, spoke in dispraise of the Dharma (dhamma), and spoke in dispraise of the Sangha (saṅgha). But Brahmadatta, the pupil of Suppiya the wanderer, spoke in many ways in praise of the Buddha, spoke in praise of the Dharma, and spoke in praise of the Sangha.

And so those two, teacher and pupil, with arguments directly opposed to each other, followed close behind the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ), followed closely (ka. sī. pī.) and the Sangha of monks (bhikkhusaṅghañca).
1. Tattha evanti nipātapadaṃ. Metiādīni nāmapadāni. Paṭipanno hotīti ettha paṭīti upasaggapadaṃ, hotīti ākhyātapadanti. Iminā tāva nayena padavibhāgo veditabbo. Atthato pana evaṃ-saddo tāva upamūpadesasampahaṃsanagarahaṇavacanasampaṭiggahākāranidassanāvadhāraṇādianekatthappabhedo. Tathāhesa – ‘‘evaṃ jātena maccena, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ bahu’’nti (dha. pa. 53) evamādīsu upamāyaṃ āgato. ‘‘Evaṃ te abhikkamitabbaṃ, evaṃ te paṭikkamitabba’’ntiādīsu (a. ni. 4.122) upadese. ‘‘Evametaṃ bhagavā, evametaṃ sugatā’’tiādīsu (a. ni. 3.66) sampahaṃsane. ‘‘Evamevaṃ panāyaṃ vasalī yasmiṃ vā tasmiṃ vā tassa muṇḍakassa samaṇakassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.187) garahaṇe. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhanteti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosu’’ntiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.1) vacanasampaṭiggahe. ‘‘Evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.398) ākāre. ‘‘Ehi tvaṃ, māṇavaka, yena samaṇo ānando tenupasaṅkama, upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena samaṇaṃ ānandaṃ appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha. ‘‘Subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhavantaṃ ānandaṃ appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’’ti. ‘‘Evañca vadehi, sādhu kira bhavaṃ ānando yena subhassa māṇavassa todeyyaputtassa nivesanaṃ, tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.445) nidassane. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, kālāmā, ime dhammā kusalā vā akusalā vāti? Akusalā, bhante. Sāvajjā vā anavajjā vāti? Sāvajjā, bhante. Viññugarahitā vā viññuppasatthā vāti? Viññugarahitā, bhante. Samattā samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattanti no vā, kathaṃ vo ettha hotīti? Samattā, bhante, samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattanti, evaṃ no ettha hotī’’tiādīsu (a. ni. 3.66) avadhāraṇe. Svāyamidha ākāranidassanāvadhāraṇesu daṭṭhabbo. Tattha ākāratthena evaṃ-saddena etamatthaṃ dīpeti, nānānayanipuṇamanekajjhāsayasamuṭṭhānaṃ, atthabyañjanasampannaṃ, vividhapāṭihāriyaṃ, dhammatthadesanāpaṭivedhagambhīraṃ, sabbasattānaṃ sakasakabhāsānurūpato sotapathamāgacchantaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ sabbappakārena ko samattho viññātuṃ, sabbathāmena pana sotukāmataṃ janetvāpi ‘evaṃ me sutaṃ’ mayāpi ekenākārena sutanti. Nidassanatthena – ‘‘nāhaṃ sayambhū, na mayā idaṃ sacchikata’’nti attānaṃ parimocento – ‘evaṃ me sutaṃ’, ‘mayāpi evaṃ suta’nti idāni vattabbaṃ sakalaṃ suttaṃ nidasseti. Avadhāraṇatthena – ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahussutānaṃ yadidaṃ ānando, gatimantānaṃ, satimantānaṃ, dhitimantānaṃ, upaṭṭhākānaṃ yadidaṃ ānando’’ti (a. ni. 1.223). Evaṃ bhagavatā – ‘‘āyasmā ānando atthakusalo, dhammakusalo, byañjanakusalo, niruttikusalo, pubbāparakusalo’’ti (a. ni. 5.169). Evaṃ dhammasenāpatinā ca pasatthabhāvānurūpaṃ attano dhāraṇabalaṃ dassento sattānaṃ sotukāmataṃ janeti – ‘evaṃ me sutaṃ’, tañca kho atthato vā byañjanato vā anūnamanadhikaṃ, evameva na aññathā daṭṭhabba’’nti. Me-saddo tīsu atthesu dissati. Tathā hissa – ‘‘gāthābhigītaṃ me abhojaneyya’’ntiādīsu (su. ni. 81) mayāti attho. ‘‘Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṃ desetū’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 4.88) mayhanti attho. ‘‘Dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave , bhavathā’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.29) mamāti attho. Idha pana mayā sutanti ca, mama sutanti ca atthadvaye yujjati. Sutanti ayaṃ suta-saddo saupasaggo ca anupasaggo ca – gamanavissutakilinna-upacitānuyoga-sotaviññeyya-sotadvārānusāra-viññātādianekatthappabhedo, tathā hissa ‘‘senāya pasuto’’tiādīsu gacchantoti attho. ‘‘Sutadhammassa passato’’tiādīsu (udā. 11) vissutadhammassāti attho. ‘‘Avassutā avassutassā’’tiādīsu (pāci. 657) kilinnākilinnassāti attho. ‘‘Tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappaka’’ntiādīsu (khu. pā. 7.12) upacitanti attho. ‘‘Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā’’tiādīsu (dha. pa. 181) jhānānuyuttāti attho. ‘Diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ muta’ntiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.241) sotaviññeyyanti attho. ‘‘Sutadharo sutasannicayo’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.339) sotadvārānusāraviññātadharoti attho. Idha panassa sotadvārānusārena upadhāritanti vā upadhāraṇanti vāti attho. ‘Me’ saddassa hi ‘mayā’ti atthe sati ‘evaṃ mayā sutaṃ’ sotadvārānusārena upadhāritanti yujjati. ‘Mamā’ti atthe sati evaṃ mama sutaṃ sotadvārānusārena upadhāraṇanti yujjati. Evametesu tīsu padesu evanti sotaviññāṇādiviññāṇakiccanidassanaṃ. Meti vuttaviññāṇasamaṅgipuggalanidassanaṃ. Sutanti assavanabhāvapaṭikkhepato anūnādhikāviparītaggahaṇanidassanaṃ. Tathā evanti tassā sotadvārānusārena pavattāya viññāṇavīthiyā nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattibhāvappakāsanaṃ. Meti attappakāsanaṃ. Sutanti dhammappakāsanaṃ. Ayañhettha saṅkhepo – ‘‘nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattāya viññāṇavīthiyā mayā na aññaṃ kataṃ, idaṃ pana kataṃ, ayaṃ dhammo suto’’ti. Tathā evanti niddisitabbadhammappakāsanaṃ. Meti puggalappakāsanaṃ. Sutanti puggalakiccappakāsanaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti. ‘‘Yaṃ suttaṃ niddisissāmi, taṃ mayā evaṃ suta’’nti. Tathā evanti yassa cittasantānassa nānākārappavattiyā nānatthabyañjanaggahaṇaṃ hoti, tassa nānākāraniddeso. Evanti hi ayamākārapaññatti. Meti kattuniddeso. Sutanti visayaniddeso. Ettāvatā nānākārappavattena cittasantānena taṃ samaṅgino kattu visayaggahaṇasanniṭṭhānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Athavā evanti puggalakiccaniddeso. Sutanti viññāṇakiccaniddeso. Meti ubhayakiccayuttapuggalaniddeso. Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, ‘‘mayā savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅginā puggalena viññāṇavasena laddhasavanakiccavohārena suta’’nti. Tattha evanti ca meti ca saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasena avijjamānapaññatti. Kiñhettha taṃ paramatthato atthi, yaṃ evanti vā meti vā niddesaṃ labhetha? Sutanti vijjamānapaññatti. Yañhi taṃ ettha sotena upaladdhaṃ, taṃ paramatthato vijjamānanti. Tathā ‘eva’nti ca, meti ca, taṃ taṃ upādāya vattabbato upādāpaññatti. ‘Suta’nti diṭṭhādīni upanidhāya vattabbato upanidhāpaññatti. Ettha ca evanti vacanena asammohaṃ dīpeti. Na hi sammūḷho nānappakārapaṭivedhasamattho hoti. ‘Suta’nti vacanena sutassa asammosaṃ dīpeti. Yassa hi sutaṃ sammuṭṭhaṃ hoti, na so kālantarena mayā sutanti paṭijānāti. Iccassa asammohena paññāsiddhi, asammosena pana satisiddhi. Tattha paññāpubbaṅgamāya satiyā byañjanāvadhāraṇasamatthatā, satipubbaṅgamāya paññāya atthapaṭivedhasamatthatā. Tadubhayasamatthatāyogena atthabyañjanasampannassa dhammakosassa anupālanasamatthato dhammabhaṇḍāgārikattasiddhi. Aparo nayo, evanti vacanena yoniso manasikāraṃ dīpeti. Ayoniso manasikaroto hi nānappakārapaṭivedhābhāvato. Sutanti vacanena avikkhepaṃ dīpeti, vikkhittacittassa savanābhāvato. Tathā hi vikkhittacitto puggalo sabbasampattiyā vuccamānopi ‘‘na mayā sutaṃ, puna bhaṇathā’’ti bhaṇati. Yoniso manasikārena cettha attasammāpaṇidhiṃ pubbe ca katapuññataṃ sādheti, sammā appaṇihitattassa pubbe akatapuññassa vā tadabhāvato. Avikkhepena saddhammassavanaṃ sappurisūpanissayañca sādheti. Na hi vikkhittacitto sotuṃ sakkoti, na ca sappurise anupassayamānassa savanaṃ atthīti. Aparo nayo, yasmā evanti yassa cittasantānassa nānākārappavattiyā nānatthabyañjanaggahaṇaṃ hoti, tassa nānākāraniddesoti vuttaṃ, so ca evaṃ bhaddako ākāro na sammāappaṇihitattano pubbe akatapuññassa vā hoti, tasmā evanti iminā bhaddakenākārena pacchimacakkadvayasampattimattano dīpeti. Sutanti savanayogena purimacakkadvayasampattiṃ. Na hi appatirūpadese vasato sappurisūpanissayavirahitassa vā savanaṃ atthi. Iccassa pacchimacakkadvayasiddhiyā āsayasuddhisiddhā hoti, purimacakkadvayasiddhiyā payogasuddhi, tāya ca āsayasuddhiyā adhigamabyattisiddhi, payogasuddhiyā āgamabyattisiddhi. Iti payogāsayasuddhassa āgamādhigamasampannassa vacanaṃ aruṇuggaṃ viya sūriyassa udayato yoniso manasikāro viya ca kusalakammassa arahati bhagavato vacanassa pubbaṅgamaṃ bhavitunti ṭhāne nidānaṃ ṭhapento – ‘‘evaṃ me suta’’ntiādimāha. Aparo nayo, ‘eva’nti iminā nānappakārapaṭivedhadīpakena vacanena attano atthapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidāsampattisabbhāvaṃ dīpeti. ‘Suta’nti iminā sotabbappabhedapaṭivedhadīpakena dhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāsampattisabbhāvaṃ. ‘Eva’nti ca idaṃ yoniso manasikāradīpakaṃ vacanaṃ bhāsamāno – ‘‘ete mayā dhammā manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā’’ti dīpeti. ‘Suta’nti idaṃ savanayogadīpakaṃ vacanaṃ bhāsamāno – ‘‘bahū mayā dhammā sutā dhātā vacasā paricitā’’ti dīpeti. Tadubhayenāpi atthabyañjanapāripūriṃ dīpento savane ādaraṃ janeti. Atthabyañjanaparipuṇṇañhi dhammaṃ ādarena assuṇanto mahatā hitā paribāhiro hotīti, tasmā ādaraṃ janetvā sakkaccaṃ ayaṃ dhammo sotabboti. ‘‘Evaṃ me suta’’nti iminā pana sakalena vacanena āyasmā ānando tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammaṃ attano adahanto asappurisabhūmiṃ atikkamati. Sāvakattaṃ paṭijānanto sappurisabhūmiṃ okkamati. Tathā asaddhammā cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti, saddhamme cittaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti. ‘‘Kevalaṃ sutamevetaṃ mayā, tasseva bhagavato vacana’’nti dīpento attānaṃ parimoceti, satthāraṃ apadisati, jinavacanaṃ appeti, dhammanettiṃ patiṭṭhāpeti. Apica ‘‘evaṃ me suta’’nti attanā uppāditabhāvaṃ appaṭijānanto purimavacanaṃ vivaranto – ‘‘sammukhā paṭiggahitamidaṃ mayā tassa bhagavato catuvesārajjavisāradassa dasabaladharassa āsabhaṭṭhānaṭṭhāyino sīhanādanādino sabbasattuttamassa dhammissarassa dhammarājassa dhammādhipatino dhammadīpassa dhammasaraṇassa saddhammavaracakkavattino sammāsambuddhassa vacanaṃ, na ettha atthe vā dhamme vā pade vā byañjane vā kaṅkhā vā vimati vā kātabbā’’ti sabbesaṃ devamanussānaṃ imasmiṃ dhamme assaddhiyaṃ vināseti, saddhāsampadaṃ uppādeti. Tenetaṃ vuccati – Ekanti gaṇanaparicchedaniddeso. Samayanti paricchinnaniddeso. Ekaṃ samayanti aniyamitaparidīpanaṃ. Tattha samayasaddo – Tathā hissa – ‘‘appevanāma svepi upasaṅkameyyāma kālañca samayañca upādāyā’’ti evamādīsu (dī. ni. 1.447) samavāyo attho. ‘‘Ekova kho bhikkhave, khaṇo ca samayo ca brahmacariyavāsāyā’’tiādīsu (a. ni. 8.29) khaṇo. ‘‘Uṇhasamayo pariḷāhasamayo’’tiādīsu (pāci. 358) kālo. ‘‘Mahāsamayo pavanasmi’’ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.332) samūho. ‘‘Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi, bhagavā kho sāvatthiyaṃ viharati, bhagavāpi maṃ jānissati, bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho, te bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.135) hetu. ‘‘Tena kho pana samayena uggahamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto samayappavādake tindukācīre ekasālake mallikāya ārāme paṭivasatī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.260) diṭṭhi. Tattha kiñcāpi etesu saṃvaccharādīsu samayesu yaṃ yaṃ suttaṃ yasmiṃ yasmiṃ saṃvacchare utumhi māse pakkhe rattibhāge vā divasabhāge vā vuttaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ therassa suviditaṃ suvavatthāpitaṃ paññāya. Yasmā pana – ‘‘evaṃ me sutaṃ’’ asukasaṃvacchare asukautumhi asukamāse asukapakkhe asukarattibhāge asukadivasabhāge vāti evaṃ vutte na sakkā sukhena dhāretuṃ vā uddisituṃ vā uddisāpetuṃ vā, bahu ca vattabbaṃ hoti, tasmā ekeneva padena tamatthaṃ samodhānetvā ‘‘ekaṃ samaya’’nti āha. Ye vā ime gabbhokkantisamayo, jātisamayo, saṃvegasamayo, abhinikkhamanasamayo, dukkarakārikasamayo, māravijayasamayo, abhisambodhisamayo diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārasamayo, desanāsamayo, parinibbānasamayoti, evamādayo bhagavato devamanussesu ativiya pakāsā anekakālappabhedā eva samayā. Tesu samayesu desanāsamayasaṅkhātaṃ ekaṃ samayanti dīpeti. Yo cāyaṃ ñāṇakaruṇākiccasamayesu karuṇākiccasamayo, attahitaparahitapaṭipattisamayesu parahitapaṭipattisamayo, sannipatitānaṃ karaṇīyadvayasamayesu dhammikathāsamayo desanāpaṭipattisamayesu desanāsamayo, tesupi samayesu aññataraṃ samayaṃ sandhāya ‘‘ekaṃ samaya’’nti āha. Kasmā panettha yathā abhidhamme ‘‘yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacara’’nti (dha. sa. 1) ca, ito aññesu ca suttapadesu – ‘‘yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehī’’ti ca bhummavacananiddeso kato, vinaye ca – ‘‘tena samayena buddho bhagavā’’ti karaṇavacanena, tathā akatvā ‘‘ekaṃ samaya’’nti upayogavacananiddeso katoti? Tattha tathā idha ca aññathā atthasambhavato. Tattha hi abhidhamme ito aññesu suttapadesu ca adhikaraṇattho bhāvena bhāvalakkhaṇattho ca sambhavati. Adhikaraṇañhi kālattho, samūhattho ca samayo, tattha tattha vuttānaṃ phassādidhammānaṃ khaṇasamavāyahetusaṅkhātassa ca samayassa bhāvena tesaṃ bhāvo lakkhīyati, tasmā tadatthajotanatthaṃ tattha bhummavacananiddeso kato. Vinaye ca hetuattho karaṇattho ca sambhavati. Yo hi so sikkhāpadapaññattisamayo sāriputtādīhipi dubbiññeyyo, tena samayena hetubhūtena karaṇabhūtena ca sikkhāpadāni paññāpayanto sikkhāpadapaññattihetuñca apekkhamāno bhagavā tattha tattha vihāsi, tasmā tadatthajotanatthaṃ tattha karaṇavacanena niddeso kato. Idha pana aññasmiñca evaṃ jātike accantasaṃyogattho sambhavati. Yañhi samayaṃ bhagavā imaṃ aññaṃ vā suttantaṃ desesi, accantameva taṃ samayaṃ karuṇāvihārena vihāsi, tasmā tadatthajotanatthaṃ idha upayogavacananiddeso katoti. Tenetaṃ vuccati – Porāṇā pana vaṇṇayanti – ‘‘tasmiṃ samaye’’ti vā, ‘‘tena samayenā’’ti vā, ‘‘ekaṃ samaya’’nti vā, abhilāpamattabhedo esa, sabbattha bhummamevatthoti. Tasmā ‘‘ekaṃ samaya’’nti vuttepi ‘‘ekasmiṃ samaye’’ti attho veditabbo. Bhagavāti garu. Garuñhi loke bhagavāti vadanti. Ayañca sabbaguṇavisiṭṭhatāya sabbasattānaṃ garu, tasmā bhagavāti veditabbo. Porāṇehipi vuttaṃ – Api ca – Imissā gāthāya vasenassa padassa vitthāraattho veditabbo. So ca visuddhimagge buddhānussatiniddese vuttoyeva. Ettāvatā cettha evaṃ me sutanti vacanena yathāsutaṃ dhammaṃ dassento bhagavato dhammakāyaṃ paccakkhaṃ karoti. Tena ‘‘nayidaṃ atikkantasatthukaṃ pāvacanaṃ, ayaṃ vo satthā’’ti satthu adassanena ukkaṇṭhitaṃ janaṃ samassāseti. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavāti vacanena tasmiṃ samaye bhagavato avijjamānabhāvaṃ dassento rūpakāyaparinibbānaṃ sādheti. Tena ‘‘evaṃvidhassa nāma ariyadhammassa desako dasabaladharo vajirasaṅghāta samānakāyo sopi bhagavā parinibbuto, kena aññena jīvite āsā janetabbā’’ti jīvitamadamattaṃ janaṃ saṃvejeti, saddhamme cassa ussāhaṃ janeti. Evanti ca bhaṇanto desanāsampattiṃ niddisati. Me sutanti sāvakasampattiṃ. Ekaṃ samayanti kālasampattiṃ. Bhagavāti desakasampattiṃ. Antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca nāḷandanti antarā-saddo kāraṇakhaṇacittavemajjhavivarādīsu dissati. ‘‘Tadantaraṃ ko jāneyya aññatra tathāgatā’’ti (a. ni. 6.44) ca, ‘‘janā saṅgamma mantenti mañca tañca kimantara’’nti (saṃ. ni. 1.228) ca ādīsu hi kāraṇe antarā-saddo. ‘‘Addasa maṃ, bhante, aññatarā itthī vijjantarikāya bhājanaṃ dhovantī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.149) khaṇe. ‘‘Yassantarato na santi kopā’’tiādīsu (udā. 20) citte. ‘‘Antarā vosānamāpādī’’tiādīsu (cūḷava. 350) vemajjhe. ‘‘Api cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, tapodā dvinnaṃ mahānirayānaṃ antarikāya āgacchatī’’tiādīsu (pārā. 231) vivare. Svāyamidha vivare vattati, tasmā rājagahassa ca nāḷandāya ca vivareti evametthattho veditabbo. Antarā-saddena pana yuttattā upayogavacanaṃ kataṃ. Īdisesu ca ṭhānesu akkharacintakā ‘‘antarā gāmañca nadiñca yātī’’ti evaṃ ekameva antarāsaddaṃ payujjanti, so dutiyapadenapi yojetabbo hoti, ayojiyamāne upayogavacanaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Idha pana yojetvāyeva vuttoti. Addhānamaggappaṭipannohotīti addhānasaṅkhātaṃ maggaṃ paṭipanno hoti, ‘‘dīghamagga’’nti attho. Addhānagamanasamayassa hi vibhaṅge ‘‘aḍḍhayojanaṃ gacchissāmīti bhuñjitabba’’ntiādivacanato (pāci. 218) aḍḍhayojanampi addhānamaggo hoti. Rājagahato pana nāḷandā yojanameva. Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhinti ‘mahatā’ti guṇamahattenapi mahatā, saṅkhyāmahattenapi mahatā. So hi bhikkhusaṅgho guṇehipi mahā ahosi, appicchatādiguṇasamannāgatattā. Saṅkhyāyapi mahā, pañcasatasaṅkhyattā. Bhikkhūnaṃ saṅgho ‘bhikkhusaṅgho’, tena bhikkhusaṅghena. Diṭṭhisīlasāmaññasaṅghātasaṅkhātena samaṇagaṇenāti attho. Saddhinti ekato. Pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehīti pañcamattā etesanti pañcamattāni. Mattāti pamāṇaṃ vuccati, tasmā yathā ‘‘bhojane mattaññū’’ti vutte ‘‘bhojane mattaṃ jānāti, pamāṇaṃ jānātī’’ti attho hoti, evamidhāpi – ‘‘tesaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ pañcamattā pañcapamāṇa’’nti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Bhikkhūnaṃ satāni bhikkhusatāni, tehi pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Suppiyopikho paribbājakoti suppiyoti tassa nāmaṃ. Pi-kāro maggappaṭipannasabhāgatāya puggalasampiṇḍanattho. Kho-kāro padasandhikaro, byañjanasiliṭṭhatāvasena vutto. Paribbājakoti sañjayassa antevāsī channaparibbājako. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘yadā bhagavā taṃ addhānamaggaṃ paṭipanno, tadā suppiyopi paribbājako paṭipanno ahosī’’ti. Atītakālattho hettha hoti-saddo. Saddhiṃ antevāsinā brahmadattena māṇavenāti – ettha ante vasatīti antevāsī. Samīpacāro santikāvacaro sissoti attho. Brahmadattoti tassa nāmaṃ. Māṇavoti sattopi coropi taruṇopi vuccati. Tatrāti tasmiṃ addhānamagge, tesu vā dvīsu janesu. Sudanti nipātamattaṃ. Anekapariyāyenāti pariyāya-saddo tāva vāradesanākāraṇesu vattati. ‘‘Kassa nu kho, ānanda, ajja pariyāyo bhikkhuniyo ovaditu’’ntiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.398) hi vāre pariyāyasaddo vattati. ‘‘Madhupiṇḍikapariyāyotveva naṃ dhārehī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.205) desanāyaṃ. ‘‘Imināpi kho, te rājañña, pariyāyena evaṃ hotū’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.411) kāraṇe. Svāyamidhāpi kāraṇe vattati, tasmā ayamettha attho – ‘‘anekavidhena kāraṇenā’’ti, ‘‘bahūhi kāraṇehī’’ti vuttaṃ hoti. Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti avaṇṇavirahitassa aparimāṇavaṇṇasamannāgatassāpi buddhassa bhagavato – ‘‘yaṃ loke jātivuḍḍhesu kattabbaṃ abhivādanādisāmīcikammaṃ ‘sāmaggiraso’ti vuccati, taṃ samaṇassa gotamassa natthi tasmā arasarūpo samaṇo gotamo, nibbhogo, akiriyavādo, ucchedavādo, jegucchī, venayiko, tapassī, apagabbho. Natthi samaṇassa gotamassa uttarimanussadhammo alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso. Takkapariyāhataṃ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ, sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ. Samaṇo gotamo na sabbaññū, na lokavidū, na anuttaro, na aggapuggalo’’ti. Evaṃ taṃ taṃ akāraṇameva kāraṇanti vatvā tathā tathā avaṇṇaṃ dosaṃ nindaṃ bhāsati. Yathā ca buddhassa, evaṃ dhammassāpi taṃ taṃ akāraṇameva kāraṇato vatvā – ‘‘samaṇassa gotamassa dhammo durakkhāto, duppaṭivedito, aniyyāniko, anupasamasaṃvattaniko’’ti tathā tathā avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Yathā ca dhammassa, evaṃ saṅghassāpi yaṃ vā taṃ vā akāraṇameva kāraṇato vatvā – ‘‘micchāpaṭipanno samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakasaṅgho, kuṭilapaṭipanno, paccanīkapaṭipadaṃ ananulomapaṭipadaṃ adhammānulomapaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno’’ti tathā tathā avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Antevāsī panassa – ‘‘amhākaṃ ācariyo aparāmasitabbaṃ parāmasati, anakkamitabbaṃ akkamati, svāyaṃ aggiṃ gilanto viya, hatthena asidhāraṃ parāmasanto viya, muṭṭhinā sineruṃ padāletukāmo viya, kakacadantapantiyaṃ kīḷamāno viya, pabhinnamadaṃ caṇḍahatthiṃ hatthena gaṇhanto viya ca vaṇṇārahasseva ratanattayassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsamāno anayabyasanaṃ pāpuṇissati. Ācariye kho pana gūthaṃ vā aggiṃ vā kaṇṭakaṃ vā kaṇhasappaṃ vā akkamante, sūlaṃ vā abhirūhante, halāhalaṃ vā visaṃ khādante, khārodakaṃ vā pakkhalante, narakapapātaṃ vā papatante, na antevāsinā taṃ sabbamanukātabbaṃ hoti. Kammassakā hi sattā attano kammānurūpameva gatiṃ gacchanti. Neva pitā puttassa kammena gacchati, na putto pitu kammena, na mātā puttassa, na putto mātuyā, na bhātā bhaginiyā, na bhaginī bhātu, na ācariyo antevāsino, na antevāsī ācariyassa kammena gacchati. Mayhañca ācariyo tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, mahāsāvajjo kho panāriyūpavādoti. Evaṃ yoniso ummujjitvā ācariyavādaṃ maddamāno sammākāraṇameva kāraṇato apadisanto anekapariyāyena tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ vaṇṇaṃ bhāsitumāraddho, yathā taṃ paṇḍitajātiko kulaputto’’. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘suppiyassa pana paribbājakassa antevāsī brahmadatto māṇavo anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī’’ti. Tattha vaṇṇanti vaṇṇa-saddo saṇṭhāna-jāti-rūpāyatana-kāraṇa-pamāṇa-guṇa-pasaṃsādīsu dissati . Tattha ‘‘mahantaṃ sapparājavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.142) saṇṭhānaṃ vuccati. ‘‘Brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.402) jāti. ‘‘Paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.303) rūpāyatanaṃ. Itiha te ubho ācariyantevāsīti evaṃ te dve ācariyantevāsikā. Aññamaññassāti añño aññassa. Ujuvipaccanīkavādāti īsakampi apariharitvā ujumeva vividhapaccanīkavādā, anekavāraṃ viruddhavādā eva hutvāti attho. Ācariyena hi ratanattayassa avaṇṇe bhāsite antevāsī vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, puna itaro avaṇṇaṃ, itaro vaṇṇanti evaṃ ācariyo sāraphalake visarukkhaāṇiṃ ākoṭayamāno viya punappunaṃ ratanattayassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Antevāsī pana suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimayāya āṇiyā taṃ āṇiṃ paṭibāhayamāno viya punappunaṃ ratanattayassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘ujuvipaccanīkavādā’’ti. Bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti bhikkhusaṅghañcāti bhagavantañca bhikkhusaṅghañca pacchato pacchato dassanaṃ avijahantā iriyāpathānubandhanena anubandhā honti, sīsānulokino hutvā anugatā hontīti attho. Kasmā pana bhagavā taṃ addhānaṃ paṭipanno? Kasmā ca suppiyo anubandho? Kasmā ca so ratanattayassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti? Bhagavā tāva tasmiṃ kāle rājagahaparivattakesu aṭṭhārasasu mahāvihāresu aññatarasmiṃ vasitvā pātova sarīrappaṭijagganaṃ katvā bhikkhācāravelāyaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto rājagahe piṇḍāya carati. So taṃ divasaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa sulabhapiṇḍapātaṃ katvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pattacīvaraṃ gāhāpetvā – ‘‘nāḷandaṃ gamissāmī’’ti, rājagahato nikkhamitvā taṃ addhānaṃ paṭipanno. Suppiyopi kho tasmiṃ kāle rājagahaparivattake aññatarasmiṃ paribbājakārāme vasitvā paribbājakaparivuto rājagahe bhikkhāya carati. Sopi taṃ divasaṃ paribbājakaparisāya sulabhabhikkhaṃ katvā bhuttapātarāso paribbājake paribbājakaparikkhāraṃ gāhāpetvā – nāḷandaṃ gamissāmicceva bhagavato taṃ maggaṃ paṭipannabhāvaṃ ajānantova anubandho. Sace pana jāneyya nānubandheyya. So ajānitvāva gacchanto gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā olokayamāno bhagavantaṃ addasa buddhasiriyā sobhamānaṃ rattakambalaparikkhittamiva jaṅgamakanakagirisikharaṃ. Tasmiṃ kira samaye dasabalassa sarīrato nikkhamitvā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo samantā asītihatthappamāṇe padese ādhāvanti vidhāvanti ratanāveḷaratanadāmaratanacuṇṇavippakiṇṇaṃ viya, pasāritaratanacittakañcanapaṭamiva, rattasuvaṇṇarasanisiñcamānamiva, ukkāsatanipātasamākulamiva, nirantaravippakiṇṇakaṇikārapupphamiva vāyuvegakkhittacīnapiṭṭhacuṇṇamiva, indadhanuvijjulatātārāgaṇappabhāvisaravipphuritaviccharitamiva ca taṃ vanantaraṃ hoti. Asīti anubyañjanānurañjitañca pana bhagavato sarīraṃ vikasitakamaluppalamiva, saraṃ sabbapāliphullamiva pāricchattakaṃ, tārāmarīcivikasitamiva, gaganatalaṃ siriyā avahasantamiva, byāmappabhāparikkhepavilāsinī cassa dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇamālā ganthetvā ṭhapitadvattiṃsacandamālāya dvattiṃsasūriyamālāya paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitadvattiṃsacakkavattidvattiṃsasakkadevarājadvattiṃsamahābrahmānaṃ siriṃ siriyā abhibhavantimiva. Tañca pana bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā ṭhitā bhikkhū sabbeva appicchā santuṭṭhā pavivittā asaṃsaṭṭhā codakā pāpagarahino vattāro vacanakkhamā sīlasampannā samādhipaññāvimuttivimuttiññāṇadassanasampannā. Tesaṃ majjhe bhagavā rattakambalapākāraparikkhitto viya kañcanathambho, rattapadumasaṇḍamajjhagatā viya suvaṇṇanāvā, pavāḷavedikāparikkhitto viya aggikkhandho, tārāgaṇaparivārito viya puṇṇacando migapakkhīnampi cakkhūni pīṇayati, pageva devamanussānaṃ. Tasmiñca pana divase yebhuyyena asītimahātherā meghavaṇṇaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ ekaṃsaṃ karitvā kattaradaṇḍaṃ ādāya suvammavammitā viya gandhahatthino vigatadosā vantadosā bhinnakilesā vijaṭitajaṭā chinnabandhanā bhagavantaṃ parivārayiṃsu. So sayaṃ vītarāgo vītarāgehi, sayaṃ vītadoso vītadosehi, sayaṃ vītamoho vītamohehi, sayaṃ vītataṇho vītataṇhehi, sayaṃ nikkileso nikkilesehi, sayaṃ buddho anubuddhehi parivārito; pattaparivāritaṃ viya kesaraṃ, kesaraparivāritā viya kaṇṇikā, aṭṭhanāgasahassaparivārito viya chaddanto nāgarājā, navutihaṃsasahassaparivārito viya dhataraṭṭho haṃsarājā, senaṅgaparivārito viya cakkavattirājā, devagaṇaparivārito viya sakko devarājā, brahmagaṇaparivārito viya hārito mahābrahmā, aparimitakālasañcitapuññabalanibbattāya acinteyyāya anopamāya buddhalīlāya cando viya gaganatalaṃ taṃ maggaṃ paṭipanno hoti. Athevaṃ bhagavantaṃ anopamāya buddhalīlāya gacchantaṃ bhikkhū ca okkhittacakkhū santindriye santamānase uparinabhe ṭhitaṃ puṇṇacandaṃ viya bhagavantaṃyeva namassamāne disvāva paribbājako attano parisaṃ avalokesi. Sā hoti kājadaṇḍake olambetvā gahitoluggaviluggapiṭṭhakatidaṇḍamorapiñchamattikāpattapasibbakakuṇḍikādianekaparikkhārabhārabharitā . ‘‘Asukassa hatthā sobhaṇā, asukassa pādā’’ti evamādiniratthakavacanā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā adassanīyā apāsādikā. Tassa taṃ disvā vippaṭisāro udapādi. Idāni tena bhagavato vaṇṇo vattabbo bhaveyya. Yasmā panesa lābhasakkārahāniyā ceva pakkhahāniyā ca niccampi bhagavantaṃ usūyati. Aññatitthiyānañhi yāva buddho loke nuppajjati, tāvadeva lābhasakkārā nibbattanti, buddhuppādato pana paṭṭhāya parihīnalābhasakkārā honti , sūriyuggamane khajjopanakā viya nissirīkataṃ āpajjanti. Upatissakolitānañca sañjayassa santike pabbajitakāleyeva paribbājakā mahāparisā ahesuṃ, tesu pana pakkantesu sāpi tesaṃ parisā bhinnā. Iti imehi dvīhi kāraṇehi ayaṃ paribbājako yasmā niccampi bhagavantaṃ usūyati, tasmā taṃ usūyavisuggāraṃ uggiranto ratanattayassa avaṇṇameva bhāsatīti veditabbo.
1. There, evaṃ is a particle.
Meti and others are nouns.
In "he has undertaken," paṭi- is a prefix, and hoti is a verb.
In this way, the division of words should be understood.
In meaning, however, the word evaṃ has various meanings, such as comparison, instruction, praise, reproach, acceptance of a statement, mode, demonstration, and ascertainment.
Likewise, it was said, "Having been born thus, a mortal should do much good" (Dha.
p.
53), it comes in comparison and so on.
"Thus should you move forward, thus should you move backward" and so on (A.
N.

"So it is, Blessed One, so it is, Well-Gone" and so on (A.
N.

66) in praise.
"Thus, in this way, this wretched woman praises that shaven ascetic, whatever or whoever he may be" and so on (Saṃ.

398) in mode.
"Come, young man, go to the śramaṇa Ānanda; having gone, ask the śramaṇa Ānanda in my name whether he is free from affliction, free from ailment, quickly rising, strong, and living in comfort.
"Subha, the young man Todeyyaputta, asks the venerable Ānanda whether he is free from affliction, free from ailment, quickly rising, strong, and living in comfort."
"And say thus: 'May the venerable Ānanda, out of compassion, come to the dwelling of Subha, the young man Todeyyaputta,'" and so on (D.

445) in demonstration.
"What do you think, O Kālāmas, are these things wholesome kuśala or unwholesome akuśala?" "Unwholesome akuśala, venerable sir."
"Are they blameworthy sāvajja or blameless anavajja?" "Blameworthy sāvajja, venerable sir."
"Are they censured by the wise viññugarahita or praised by the wise viññuppasattha?" "Censured by the wise viññugarahita, venerable sir."
"Being undertaken and put into effect, do they lead to harm and suffering duḥkha, or not, or how does it appear to you in this case?" "Being undertaken and put into effect, venerable sir, they lead to harm and suffering duḥkha; thus it appears to us in this case" and so on (A.
N.
3.66) In the sense of emphasis.

Here, it should be viewed as an instance of mode, illustration and emphasis.

Herein, in the sense of mode, he illustrates this meaning by the word "thus". [The meaning is that the Blessed One's word] is skillful in many methods (nānānayanipuṇa), arises from diverse inclinations (anekajjhāsayasamuṭṭhānaṃ), is endowed with meaning and expression (atthabyañjanasampannaṃ), possesses various marvels (vividhapāṭihāriyaṃ), is profound in teaching and penetrating ideas and meanings (dhammatthadesanāpaṭivedhagambhīraṃ), and comes to the ear of all beings (sabbasattānaṃ) in accordance with their own language (sakasakabhāsānurūpato). Who is capable of understanding it in every way (sabbappakārena)? However, by arousing the desire to hear in every way (sabbathāmena), [it is said] 'Thus I heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ),' and 'I also heard (mayāpi evaṃ suta) in one way (ekena ākārena.'

In the sense of demonstration, excluding himself by saying, "I am not self-become (nāhaṃ sayambhū), nor has this been realized by me (na mayā idaṃ sacchikata)," he demonstrates the entire sūtra (sakalaṃ suttaṃ) that is to be spoken now, [saying] "Thus I heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ)," "I also heard (mayāpi evaṃ suta)."

In the sense of emphasis, [it is said,] "Monks, this Ānanda is foremost among my disciples who are learned (bahussutānaṃ), endowed with gati, sati, and dhiti, and attendants (upaṭṭhākānaṃ)," (A.N. 1.223).

Thus, by the Blessed One: “The venerable Ānanda is skilled in meaning (arthakusala), skilled in Dharma (dharmakusala), skilled in expression (byañjanakusala), skilled in etymology (niruttikusala), skilled in what precedes and what follows (pubbāparakusala)," (A.N. 5.169).

Thus, the general of the Dharma (dhammasenāpatinā), showing his strength of memory (dhāraṇabalaṃ) in accordance with the commended state (pasatthabhāvānurūpaṃ), generates a desire to hear in beings (sattānaṃ sotukāmataṃ janeti), [saying] "Thus I heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ)," and "That, indeed, is neither less nor more in meaning or expression (atthato vā byañjanato vā anūnamanadhikaṃ), and it should be regarded exactly thus (evameva na aññathā daṭṭhabba)."

The word "me" (me-saddo) appears in three senses (tīsu atthesu dissati).

Thus, in passages such as "What has been earned by stanzas is uneatable by me (gāthābhigītaṃ me abhojaneyya)," (S.N. 81) the meaning is "by me (mayā)."

In passages such as "Venerable Sir (bhante), may the Blessed One (bhagavā) teach me the Dharma (dhammaṃ desetū) in brief (saṅkhittena)," (S.N. 4.88) the meaning is "to me (mayhaṃ)."

In passages such as "Monks (bhikkhave), be my heirs in Dharma (dhammadāyādā me)," (M.N. 1.29) the meaning is "of me (mama)."

Here, however, "by me heard (mayā sutaṃ)" and "my heard (mama sutaṃ)" are appropriate in two meanings (atthadvaye yujjati).

Here, suta, this word suta, with and without prefixes (saupasaggo ca anupasaggo ca)—[has] various kinds of meanings (anekatthappabhedo), such as going, celebrated, stained, accumulated, application, knowable by the ear, following the ear-door, known, and so forth—thus, in passages such as "Urging the army (senāya pasuto)," the meaning is "going (gacchanto)."

In passages such as "Of one who sees the heard Dharma (sutadhammassa passato)," (Udā. 11) the meaning is "of the celebrated Dharma (vissutadhammassa)."

In passages such as "Flowed out, of one who has flowed out (avassutā avassutassā)," (Pāci. 657) the meaning is "of one stained and unstained (kilinnākilinnassa)."

In passages such as "Merit has been produced by you, no little (tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappaka)," (Khu. Pā. 7.12) the meaning is "accumulated (upacitaṃ)."

In passages such as "Those steadfast ones intent on jhāna (ye jhānapasutā dhīrā)," (Dha. Pa. 181) the meaning is "devoted to jhāna (jhānānuyuttā)."

ni.
1.
2. 241) sotaviññeyyanti attho: the meaning is, cognizable by the ear.
‘‘sutadharo sutasannicayo’’tiādīsu (ma.: in such passages as 'he remembers what he has heard, stores up what he has heard' (etc.).
ni.
1.
2. 339) sotadvārānusāraviññātadharoti attho: the meaning is, one who bears in mind what is cognized in the ear-door.
idha panassa sotadvārānusārena upadhāritanti vā upadhāraṇanti vāti attho: But here the meaning of sutam is properly ‘what has been recorded by a given series of consciousnesses ushered in by ear-consciousness’, or it is the ‘act of recording’.
‘me’ saddassa hi ‘mayā’ti atthe sati ‘evaṃ mayā sutaṃ’ sotadvārānusārena upadhāritanti yujjati: ‘me’ means ‘by me’; thus when there is the meaning of ‘by me’, it is fitting [to say] ‘evaṃ mayā sutaṃ’ what has been recorded by a given series of consciousnesses ushered in by ear-consciousness.
‘mamā’ti atthe sati evaṃ mama sutaṃ sotadvārānusārena upadhāraṇanti yujjati: ‘mine’ means when there is the meaning of ‘mine,’ thus ‘evaṃ mama sutaṃ’ is fitting as the act of recording by a given series of consciousnesses ushered in by ear-consciousness.
evametesu tīsu padesu evanti sotaviññāṇādiviññāṇakiccanidassanaṃ: So as regards these three words, evam is the demonstration of consciousness’s function as ear-consciousness, etc.
meti vuttaviññāṇasamaṅgipuggalanidassanaṃ: and me demonstrates a person connected with the described consciousness.
sutanti assavanabhāvapaṭikkhepato anūnādhikāviparītaggahaṇanidassanaṃ: while sutam is a demonstration of grasping what is neither deficient nor excessive nor distorted, because it rejects the state of non-hearing.
tathā evanti tassā sotadvārānusārena pavattāya viññāṇavīthiyā nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattibhāvappakāsanaṃ: Similarly, evam demonstrates that the kinds of cognizance beginning with hearing have actually occurred in the various ways with respect to an object by the description of the modes of the cognitive series 17 that has occurred by means of the ear-consciousness.
meti attappakāsanaṃ: me demonstrates an individual self.
sutanti dhammappakāsanaṃ: and sutam demonstrates an idea.
ayañhettha saṅkhepo – ‘‘nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattāya viññāṇavīthiyā mayā na aññaṃ kataṃ, idaṃ pana kataṃ, ayaṃ dhammo suto’’ti: Herein this is the summary: “Nothing else was done by me with the cognitive series that has occurred in the various ways with respect to an object; but this was done; this idea was cognized.”
tathā evanti niddisitabbadhammappakāsanaṃ: Similarly, evam demonstrates something about to be demonstrated.
meti puggalappakāsanaṃ: me demonstrates a person.
sutanti puggalakiccappakāsanaṃ: and sutam demonstrates the person’s function.
idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti: This is what is said:
‘‘yaṃ suttaṃ niddisissāmi, taṃ mayā evaṃ suta’’nti: “That sūtra which I will indicate, that was thus heard by me”.
tathā evanti yassa cittasantānassa nānākārappavattiyā nānatthabyañjanaggahaṇaṃ hoti, tassa nānākāraniddeso: Similarly, evam is the various demonstration of one whose mind-continuum has a grasp of various meanings and expressions from the occurrence of various modes.
evanti hi ayamākārapaññatti: evam is indeed the description of this mode.
meti kattuniddeso: me demonstrates an agent.
sutanti visayaniddeso: sutam demonstrates an object.
ettāvatā nānākārappavattena cittasantānena taṃ samaṅgino kattu visayaggahaṇasanniṭṭhānaṃ kataṃ hoti: To this extent, by the mind-continuum that occurs in various modes, the establishment of the agent's grasp of the object is done by him who is connected with it.
athavā evanti puggalakiccaniddeso: Or, evam demonstrates a person’s function.
sutanti viññāṇakiccaniddeso: sutam demonstrates consciousness’s function.
meti ubhayakiccayuttapuggalaniddeso: and me demonstrates a person connected with both these functions.
ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, ‘‘mayā savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅginā puggalena viññāṇavasena laddhasavanakiccavohārena suta’’nti: Herein, this is the summary, “By me, a person connected with consciousness functioning as hearing, by means of consciousness, by a term for a function of acquired hearing, [it was] cognized”.
tattha evanti ca meti ca saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasena avijjamānapaññatti: Herein, the words evam and me are, in the true sense and ultimate sense, a description in terms of the non- factual.
kiñhettha taṃ paramatthato atthi, yaṃ evanti vā meti vā niddesaṃ labhetha? sutanti vijjamānapaññatti: What, herein, exists in the ultimate sense, that could obtain a demonstration such as evam or me? while sutam is a description in terms of the factual.
yañhi taṃ ettha sotena upaladdhaṃ, taṃ paramatthato vijjamānanti: Because, indeed, that which is perceived here by the ear is, in the ultimate sense, factual.
tathā ‘eva’nti ca, meti ca, taṃ taṃ upādāya vත්තබ්ବతో upādāpaññatti: Similarly, evam and me are a derivative description because they are stated derivatively upon this or that fact.
‘suta’nti diṭṭhādīni upanidhāya vत्तබ්බతో upanidhāpaññatti: while sutam is an appositional description because it that is, the heard, is so called in apposition to the seen and the rest.
ettha ca evanti vacanena asammohaṃ dīpeti: Here too, by the word evam he points out non-confusion.
na hi sammūḷho nānappakārapaṭivedhasamattho hoti: For someone who is confused is not capable of penetration of difference in kind.
‘suta’nti vacanena sutassa asammosaṃ dīpeti: By the word sutam he points out non-forgetting of what was heard.
yassa hi sutaṃ sammuṭṭhaṃ hoti, na so kālantarena mayā sutanti paṭijānāti: Because, someone whose hearing is forgotten, does not acknowledge after a time has elapsed: ‘I heard [this]’.
Through non-confusion, there is accomplishment of wisdom (paññā-siddhi); however, through non-forgetfulness, there is accomplishment of mindfulness (sati-siddhi).

There, with mindfulness preceded by wisdom, there is the ability to ascertain the letters (byañjanāvadhāraṇa-samatthatā); with wisdom preceded by mindfulness, there is the ability to penetrate the meaning (attha-paṭivedha-samatthatā).

Through the power of both these abilities, there is accomplishment of being a custodian of the dharma-treasure (dharma-bhāṇḍāgārika-tta-siddhi), due to the ability to preserve the dharma-treasury (dharma-kośa) which is endowed with meaning and letters (attha-byañjana-sampannassa).

Another way: by the word evaṃ, he indicates reasoned attention (yoniso manasikāraṃ dīpeti).

Indeed, because of the absence of various kinds of penetration, [that comes] from not giving reasoned attention (ayoniso manasi-karoto hi nānappakāra-paṭivedhābhāvato).

By the word sutaṃ, he indicates non-distraction (avikkhepaṃ dīpeti), because hearing is absent in one whose mind is distracted (vikkhitta-cittassa savanābhāvato).

For example, a distracted person, even when being told everything, says, "I did not hear it; say it again."

And through reasoned attention (yoniso manasikārena), here he establishes right self-direction (attasammāpaṇidhiṃ) and previously performed merit (katapuññataṃ), because of the absence of that (tadabhāvato) in one who is wrongly directed (sammā appaṇihita-attassa) and has not performed merit previously (akatapuññassa vā).

Through non-distraction (avikkhepena), he establishes hearing the true dharma (saddhammassavanaṃ) and reliance on true men (sappurisūpanissayañca).

For a distracted person is not able to hear, nor is there hearing for one who does not attend upon true men.

Another way: because by evaṃ, the grasping of various meanings and letters (nānā-attha-byañjana-ggahaṇaṃ) occurs to the mind-stream (citta-santānassa) with various kinds of activity (nānākāra-ppavattiyā), therefore it is said to be a designation of various kinds (nānākāra-niddeso). But that good form (bhaddako ākāro) does not occur for one who is wrongly directed (sammā appaṇihita-attano) and has not previously performed merit (akatapuññassa vā); therefore by this good form (iminā bhaddakenākārena) he indicates the attainment of the two subsequent wheels (pacchimacakka-dvaya-sampattiṃ).

Sutaṃ [indicates] the attainment of the two prior wheels (purimacakkadvayasampattiṃ) through the practice of hearing (savana-yogena).

Indeed, there is no hearing (savanaṃ natthi) for one dwelling in an unsuitable place (appatirūpa-dese vasato) or who is without reliance on true men (sappurisūpanissaya-virahitassa vā).

Through the accomplishment of the two subsequent wheels (pacchima-cakka-dvaya-siddhiyā), there is the accomplishment of purity of intention (āśaya-śuddhi-siddhā hoti); through the accomplishment of the two prior wheels (purima-cakka-dvaya-siddhiyā), there is purity of practice (prayoga-śuddhi). And through that purity of intention (tāya ca āśaya-śuddhiyā), there is accomplishment of manifest realization (adhigama-byatti-siddhi); through purity of practice (prayoga-śuddhiyā), there is accomplishment of manifest tradition (āgama-byatti-siddhi).

Thus, the speech (vacanaṃ) of one whose practice and intention are pure (payoga-āśaya-śuddhasa) and who is endowed with tradition and realization (āgama-adhigama-sampannassa), like the first light of dawn (aruṇuggaṃ viya) from the rising of the sun (sūriyassa udayato), and like reasoned attention (yoniso manasikāro viya ca) to wholesome action (kuśala-kammassa), he establishes the cause (nidānaṃ ṭhapento) in a suitable place (ṭhāne), [saying]: "Evaṃ me sutaṃ – Thus have I heard." He said, beginning with that, that it is fitting to precede the word of the Blessed One (arhati bhagavato vacanassa pubbaṅgamaṃ bhavituṃ).

Another way: by the word evaṃ, with this word that illuminates various kinds of penetration (iminā nānāppakāra-paṭivedha-dīpakena vacanena), he indicates the complete presence of his own skillful understanding of meaning and analytical insight (attano attha-paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā-sampatti-sabbhāvaṃ dīpeti).

Sutaṃ [indicates] the complete presence of analytical insight and skillful expression of dharma in a way that illuminates the divisions of what is to be heard (sotabba-ppabheda-paṭivedha-dīpakena dhamma-nirutti-paṭisambhidā-sampatti-sabbhāvaṃ).

And evaṃ—illuminating reasoned attention (yoniso manasikāra-dīpakaṃ)—uttering the word idaṃ, he indicates: "These dharmas have been considered by me in my mind, [and] are well-penetrated by insight" (ete mayā dhammā manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā).

Sutaṃ—illuminating the practice of hearing (savana-yoga-dīpakaṃ)—uttering the word idaṃ, he indicates: "Many dharmas have been heard by me, retained, [and] consolidated by word" (bahū mayā dhammā sutā dhātā vacasā paricitā).

By both of these, showing the completeness of meaning and letter (attha-byañjana-pāripūriṃ dīpento), he generates reverence in hearing (savane ādaraṃ janeti).

For indeed, one who does not respectfully listen to the dharma that is complete in meaning and letter (attha-byañjana-paripuṇṇaṃ hi dhammaṃ ādarena assuṇanto) is excluded from great benefit (mahatā hitā paribāhiro hoti); therefore, generating reverence (ādaraṃ janetvā), this dharma should be heard carefully (sakkaccaṃ ayaṃ dhammo sotabbo).

"Thus I have heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ)"—by this entire utterance (iminā pana sakalena vacanena), the venerable Ānanda, not appropriating to himself the dharma proclaimed by the Tathāgata (tathāgata-ppaveditaṃ dhammaṃ attano adahanto), transcends the plane of those who are not true men (asappurisa-bhūmiṃ atikkamati).

Acknowledging discipleship (sāvakattaṃ paṭijānanto), he descends to the plane of true men (sappurisa-bhūmiṃ okkamati).

Thus, he has his mind emerge from what is not the true dharma (asaddhammā cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpeti), [and] he establishes his mind in the true dharma (saddhamme cittaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti).

"All this has been heard by me, [and] is the word of the Blessed One" (kevalaṃ sutam-ev-etaṃ mayā, tassa-eva bhagavato vacanaṃ)—showing this (dīpento), he frees himself (attānaṃ parimoceti), he bears witness to the Teacher (satthāraṃ apadisati), he applies the Victor's word (jinavacanaṃ appeti), [and] he establishes the guide of the dharma (dhamma-nettiṃ patiṭṭhāpeti).

Moreover, "Thus I have heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ)"—not claiming it to be produced by himself (attanā uppāditabhāvaṃ appaṭijānanto), clarifying the prior utterance (purimaṃ vacanaṃ vivaranto)—"This has been received by me directly (sammukhā paṭiggahitam idaṃ mayā) from that Blessed One who is confident in the four grounds for confidence (catu-vesārajja-visāradassa), the possessor of the ten powers (dasa-bala-dharassa), abiding in the place of a bull (āsabha-ṭṭhāna-ṭṭhāyino), with the sound of a lion's roar and so forth (sīhanāda-nādino), the best of all beings (sabba-sattu-ttamassa), the lord of the dharma (dhamm-issarassa), the king of the dharma (dhamma-rājassa), the master of the dharma (dhammādhipatino), the lamp of the dharma (dhamma-dīpassa), the refuge of the dharma (dhamma-saraṇassa), the best wheel-turner of the true dharma (saddhamma-vara-cakka-vattino), the perfectly awakened one (sammā-sambuddhassa vacanaṃ)—"Here, there should not be doubt or uncertainty (na ettha atthe vā dhamme vā pade vā byañjane vā kaṅkhā vā vimati vā kātabbā)." He destroys the lack of faith in this dharma in all gods and humans (sabbesaṃ deva-manussānaṃ imasmiṃ dhamme assaddhiyaṃ vināseti), [and] he generates the accomplishment of faith (saddhā-sampadaṃ uppādeti).

Therefore this is said: ekaṃ—a designation that is a reckoning and a demarcation (gaṇana-pariccheda-niddeso).

Samayanti—a demarcated designation (paricchinna-niddeso).

Ekaṃ samayanti—an indefinite illumination (aniyamita-paridīpanaṃ).

260) A view.
There, although in these occasions beginning with year, whatever sutta was spoken in whichever year, season, month, fortnight, night or day, all that is well-known and well-established in wisdom to the Elder.
Because, however – "Thus I have heard" in such-and-such year, in such-and-such season, in such-and-such month, in such-and-such fortnight, in such-and-such part of the night, in such-and-such part of the day – when it is said thus, it is not possible to retain it easily or to recite it, or to have it recited, and much has to be said, therefore having summarized that meaning in one word, he said "On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ).
Or else what is meant is: among the Blessed One’s several times specially evident to gods and men and counted as Occasions, such as the Occasion of the Conception in the Womb ( gabbhokkantisamaya ), Occasion of the Birth ( jātisamaya ), Occasion of the Sense of Urgency ( saṃvegasamaya ), Occasion of the Renunciation ( abhinikkhamanasamaya ), Occasion of the Austerities ( dukkarakārikāsamaya ), Occasion of the Conquest of Māra ( māravijayasamaya ), Occasion of the Enlightenment ( abhisambodhisamaya ), Occasion of the Pleasant Abiding Here and Now ( diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārasamaya ), Occasion of the Teaching ( desanāsamaya ), Occasion of the Final Extinction ( parinibbānasamaya ).
Among these occasions, he indicates that the Occasion of Teaching ( desanāsamaya ) is called "one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ).
And that occasion of compassionate action among occasions of knowledge and compassionate action, the occasion of practice beneficial to others among occasions of practice beneficial to oneself and to others, the occasion of Dhamma talk among occasions of two duties that should be done by those assembled, the occasion of teaching among occasions of practice of teaching, also with reference to those occasions, he said "On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ).
Why is the accusative case used here, as in the Abhidhamma, "when the realm of desire" ( yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ ) (Dha.
Sa.
1) and, in other Sutta passages, "when, monks, a monk is secluded from desires" ( yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi ) is the locative case used, and in the Vinaya, "at that time the Buddha, the Blessed One" ( tena samayena buddho bhagavā ) is the instrumental case used, and not having done so, why is the accusative case "On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ) used? There, it is so because the meaning is possible in different ways here and there.
For there, in the Abhidhamma and in other Sutta passages, the meaning of the locative case as a container and the meaning of characterization of one substantive by another substantive are possible.
Now the locative case is the time, and the Occasion is a collection; there, the nature of those things beginning with contact, which are stated there, is characterized by the nature of the Occasion, which is called a moment, an event, and a cause, therefore the locative case is used there to illuminate that meaning.
And in the Vinaya, the meaning of the instrumental case is that of cause and reason.
For that Occasion of the proclamation of the training precept, which is difficult to know even for Sāriputta and others, the Blessed One, making known the training precepts on that occasion, which was the cause and the reason, and expecting the cause of the proclamation of the training precept, dwelt there and there, therefore the instrumental case is used there to illuminate that meaning.
Here, however, and in other similar passages, the meaning of direct governance is possible.
For when the Blessed One taught this or any other Sutta, he dwelt on that occasion entirely in an abode of compassion, therefore the accusative case is used here to illuminate that meaning.
Therefore, it is said thus: But the ancients explain it, "At that time" ( tasmiṃ samaye ) or, "By that time" ( tena samayena ) or, "On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ), this is merely a difference in expression, the meaning is the same everywhere.
Therefore, even when "On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ) is said, the meaning should be understood as "At one occasion" ( ekasmiṃ samaye ).
Bhagavā is revered.
For in the world, they call the Bhagavā revered.
And this one is revered by all beings because of being distinguished by all qualities, therefore he should be understood as the Bhagavā.
It has also been said by the ancients – and also – the meaning of the expansion of the meaning of the word according to this verse should be understood.
And that has already been said in the section on recollection of the Buddha in the Visuddhimagga.
Thus far, by the words "Thus I have heard" here, showing the Dhamma as it was heard, he makes the Dhammakāya of the Blessed One manifest.
Therefore, by the Teacher's not being seen, he consoles the people who are longing [for him], [saying] "This is not a teaching with a passed-away teacher, this is your Teacher" ( ayaṃ vo satthā ).
By the words "On one occasion the Blessed One" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā ), showing the non-existence of the Blessed One at that time, he establishes the parinibbāna of the rūpakāya.
Therefore, "Such a one, the teacher of the noble Dhamma, the possessor of the ten powers, whose body is like a mass of diamonds, even that Blessed One has attained parinibbāna, by what other should hope be generated in life?" Thus he stirs up the people who are intoxicated with the pride of life, and he generates enthusiasm in them for the true Dhamma.
And saying "Thus" ( evaṃ ), he indicates the accomplishment of the teaching ( desanāsampattiṃ ).
"Thus I have heard" ( me sutaṃ ) is the accomplishment of a listener ( sāvakasampattiṃ ).
"On one occasion" ( ekaṃ samayaṃ ) is the accomplishment of time ( kālasampattiṃ ).
and by the words “the Exalted One,” that it possesses a teacher.
And between Rājagaha and Nāḷanda, the word antarā appears in the meanings of cause, moment, mind, middle, interval, and so on.
"Who would know that interval apart from the Tathāgatas?" (A.
Nipāta 6.
44) and, "When people meet and discuss, what is the interval between you and me?" (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.
228) and so on, the word antarā is [used] in the sense of cause.
"A certain woman saw me by a flash of lightning, O Blessed One, washing a pot" etc. (Majjhima Nikāya 2.
149) [is used in the sense of] moment.
"For whom there is no anger within" etc. (Udāna 20) [is used in the sense of] mind (citta).
"The end came in between" etc. (Cūḷavagga 350) [is used in the sense of] middle (vemajjhe).
"But the Tapodā runs between two great hells, monks" etc. (Pārājika 231) [is used in the sense of] interval (vivare).
Now, it exists in this interval, therefore, the interval between Rājagaha and Nāḷanda, thus the meaning here should be understood.
Because it is associated with the word antarā, the expression "upayoga" is made.
And in such places, those who contemplate letters use only one word antarā "he goes between the village and the river" thus, that should be connected even with the second word. If it is not connected, the expression "upayoga" is not obtained.
Here, however, it is said having connected [the words].
Addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti means he has undertaken a path known as addhāna, the meaning is "a long path".
In the analysis of the time of going on a long journey, "I will go half a yojana, therefore food should be eaten" etc. (Pācittiya 218) even half a yojana is a long journey.
Now, from Rājagaha to Nāḷanda is only one yojana.
With a great monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghena), 'great' means great by the greatness of virtue (guṇamahattena), and great by the greatness of number (saṅkhyāmahattena).
That monastic community (bhikkhusaṅgho) was great also by virtue (guṇehipi), because of being endowed with qualities such as fewness of wishes (appicchatādiguṇasamannāgatattā).
It was also great in number (saṅkhyāyapi mahā), being numbered at five hundred (pañcasatasaṅkhyattā).
The saṅgha of bhikkhus is the bhikkhusaṅgho; by that bhikkhusaṅghena.
The meaning is a community of ascetics (samaṇagaṇena) designated by agreement in views and moral conduct (diṭṭhisīlasāmaññasaṅghātasaṅkhātena).
The meaning of saddhinti is together (ekato).
By five matta hundreds of monks (bhikkhusatehīti) means those are five matta, therefore they are five mattas.
Mattā means pamāṇa is said; therefore, just as when it is said "knowing the measure in food" (bhojane mattaññū), the meaning is "he knows the measure in food, he knows the pamāṇa", thus here also – "those five matta hundreds of monks are five pamāṇas", thus the meaning should be seen.
Hundreds of monks (bhikkhūnaṃ satāni) are monk hundreds (bhikkhusatāni), by those five matta hundreds of monks (pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi).
Suppiyopikho paribbājakoti means Suppiya is his name.
The particle pi- has the meaning of combining persons due to being in the same state of having undertaken the path (maggappaṭipannasabhāgatāya puggalasampiṇḍanattho).
The particle kho- makes a connection between words (padasandhikaro), [it is] said because of the ease of consonants (byañjanasiliṭṭhatāvasena vutto).
Paribbājako means an inhabitant of Sañjaya (sañjayassa antevāsī) [is] a wanderer covered [by clothes] (channaparibbājako).
Thus it is said: "When the Blessed One set out on that long road ( addhānamagga), then Suppiya the wanderer also set out."
Here, the word hoti indicates the past tense.
Saddhiṃ antevāsinā brahmadattena māṇavenāti - antevāsī means one who dwells near.
The meaning is: a disciple is one who is in close association, who frequents the vicinity.
Brahmadatta is his name.
Māṇava can refer to a noble, a thief, or a youth.

Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti - of the Blessed Buddha, who is without fault and endowed with immeasurable virtues: "The proper duty towards the elders by birth, such as salutation and respect, is called 'the taste of concord'. The ascetic Gotama does not have this, therefore, the ascetic Gotama is without taste, worthless, an inactionist (akiriyavādo), an annihilationist (ucchedavādo), disgusting, a trainer, an ascetic, and arrogant.

The ascetic Gotama has attained no state transcending the merely human level ( uttarimanussadhamma), no distinguished knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (ariya-ñāṇa-dassana-viseso).
The ascetic Gotama teaches a dhamma merely hammered out by reasoning ( takkapariyāhataṃ), following his own line of inquiry ( vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ), as it occurs to him (sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ).
The ascetic Gotama is not omniscient (sabbaññū), not a knower of the worlds (lokavidū), not supreme (anuttaro), not the foremost individual (aggapuggalo)".
Thus, having said that the causeless is itself the cause (akāraṇameva kāraṇanti vatvā), he speaks again and again with disparagement (avaṇṇaṃ), fault (dosaṃ), and censure (nindaṃ).
Just as he spoke against the Buddha, so too against the dhamma, having said that the causeless is itself the cause (akāraṇameva kāraṇato vatvā) - "The ascetic Gotama's dhamma is wrongly expounded (durakkhāto), wrongly penetrated (duppaṭivedito), not liberating (aniyyāniko), not conducive to peace (anupasamasaṃvattaniko)" - thus, again and again, he speaks disparagingly.
Just as regarding the dhamma, so too regarding the saṅgha, having said that the causeless is itself the cause (akāraṇameva kāraṇato vatvā) - "The ascetic Gotama's community of disciples (sāvakasaṅgho) is practicing wrongly (micchāpaṭipanno), perversely (kuṭilapaṭipanno), has entered upon a warped (paccanīkapaṭipadaṃ), distorted (ananulomapaṭipadaṃ), unrighteous (adhammānulomapaṭipadaṃ) course of practice" - thus, again and again, he speaks disparagingly.
His pupil, however, [said]: "Our teacher touches what should not be touched, approaches what should not be approached; like one swallowing fire, like one touching the sharp edge of a sword with his hand, like one wanting to split Mount Meru with his fist, like one playing in a row of saw-like teeth, like one seizing a rutting, fierce elephant with his hand, so he, speaking ill of the Triple Gem (ratanattaya) worthy of praise, will incur misfortune and ruin.
If the teacher were to tread upon dung, fire, thorns, or a black snake, or to mount a stake, eat deadly poison, step into a violent stream, or throw himself down a cliff, there is no reason for the pupil to follow suit.
For beings are the owners of their kamma and they each go their own way according to their own kamma.
The father does not inherit the son’s kamma, nor the son the father’s; the mother does not inherit the son’s kamma, nor the son the mother’s; the brother does not inherit the sister’s kamma, nor the sister the brother’s; the teacher does not inherit the pupil’s kamma, nor the pupil the teacher’s.
My teacher speaks in dispraise of the Triple Gem (tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ); this is a terrible blameworthy deed—the reviling of the ariyas."
Emerging from such wise reflections, since he was a naturally intelligent young man, he began to speak in many ways in praise of the Triple Gem (tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ), confuting his teacher’s views and supporting himself with cogent reasons.
Thus it was said: "Suppiya's pupil, Brahmadatta, speaks in various ways in praise of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha."

Aññamaññassāti añño aññassa: "one another" means one for another.
Ujuvipaccanīkavādāti: īsakampi apariharitvā ujumeva vividhapaccanīkavādā, anekavāraṃ viruddhavādā eva hutvāti attho: meaning that without abandoning even a little, directly [they are] those with diverse opposing views, having many times contradictory views.
Because when dispraise (avaṇṇe) of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa) is spoken by the teacher (ācariyena), the pupil (antevāsī) speaks praise (vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati); again, the other [speaks] dispraise (avaṇṇaṃ), the other [speaks] praise (vaṇṇaṃ) - thus, the teacher, as if hammering a crooked peg (visarukkhaāṇiṃ) on a strong board (sāraphalake), repeatedly speaks dispraise (avaṇṇaṃ) of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa).
But the pupil (antevāsī), as if warding off that peg (taṃ āṇiṃ) with a peg (āṇiyā) made of gold, silver, and jewels (suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimayāya), repeatedly speaks praise (vaṇṇaṃ) of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa).
Therefore, it was said: "Ujuvipaccanīkavādā."
They followed (anubandhā honti) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) closely (piṭṭhito piṭṭhito) and the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghañcāti); not abandoning (avijahantā) the sight (dassanaṃ) of the Blessed One (bhagavantañca) and the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghañca) from behind (pacchato pacchato), they followed (anubandhā honti) with continued deportment (iriyāpathānubandhanena), meaning they went (anugatā hontīti) having become those who looked after their heads (sīsānulokino).
Why did the Blessed One (bhagavā) set out (paṭipanno) on that road (taṃ addhānaṃ)? And why did Suppiya (suppiyo) follow (anubandho)? And why did he (so) speak dispraise (avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti) of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa)? At that time (tasmiṃ kāle), the Blessed One (bhagavā), having dwelt (vasitvā) in one (aññatarasmiṃ) of the eighteen great monasteries (aṭṭhārasasu mahāvihāresu) in the vicinity of Rājagaha (rājagahaparivattakesu), early in the morning (pātova) having restored his body (sarīrappaṭijagganaṃ katvā) and at the time for the alms round (bhikkhācāravelāyaṃ), surrounded by the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto), wanders (carati) for alms (piṇḍāya) in Rājagaha (rājagaha).
Having made (katvā) an easily obtained alms-meal (sulabhapiṇḍapātaṃ) for the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghassa) on that day (taṃ divasaṃ), after the meal (pacchābhattaṃ) having returned from the alms round (piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto), having made (gāhāpetvā) the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ) bring his bowl and robe (pattacīvaraṃ) — "I will go (gamissāmi) to Nāḷanda (nāḷandaṃ)," he said (iti), having left (nikkhamitvā) Rājagaha (rājagahato) he set out (paṭipanno) on that road (taṃ addhānaṃ).
Also, Suppiya (suppiyopi), at that time (tasmiṃ kāle), having dwelt (vasitvā) in one (aññatarasmiṃ) of the monasteries (ārāme) for wanderers (paribbājakā) in the vicinity of Rājagaha (rājagahaparivattake), surrounded by wanderers (paribbājakaparivuto), wanders (carati) for alms (bhikkhāya) in Rājagaha (rājagahe).
He too (sopi), having made (katvā) an easily obtained alms-meal (sulabhabhikkhaṃ) for the wanderers' assembly (paribbājakaparisāya) on that day (taṃ divasaṃ), having finished his morning meal (bhuttapātarāso), having made (gāhāpetvā) the wanderers (paribbājake) bring his set of wanderer's requisites (paribbājakaparikkhāraṃ) - "I will go (gamissāmi) to Nāḷanda (nāḷandaṃ)," he said (icceva), not knowing (ajānantova) that the Blessed One (bhagavato) had set out (paṭipannabhāvaṃ) on that road (taṃ maggaṃ), he followed (anubandho).
If he had known (jāneyya), he would not have followed (nānubandheyya).
He, going along (gacchanto) unknowingly (ajānitvāva), having lifted his neck (gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā), looking around (olokayamāno), saw (addasa) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) shining (sobhamānaṃ) with the glory of a Buddha (buddhasiriyā), like the shimmering crest (sikharam) of a moving golden mountain (jaṅgamakanakagiriṃ) enveloped in a red woolen blanket (rattakambalaparikkhittamiva).
At that time (tasmiṃ samaye), it is said (kira), having come forth (nikkhamitvā) from the body (sarīrato) of the Ten-Powered One (dasabalassa), six-colored rays (chabbaṇṇarasmiyo), all around (samantā) in an area the size of eighty hands (asītihatthappamāṇe padese) rushed (ādhāvanti), sped (vidhāvanti), like a bejeweled courtyard (ratanāveḷa) scattered with strings of jewels (ratanadāma) and powder of jewels (ratanacuṇṇa), like a spread cloth (paṭamiva) painted with jewels (ratanacitta) and gold (kañcana), like something sprinkled with the essence of red gold (rattasuvaṇṇarasanisiñcamānamiva), like something teeming with a hundred meteors (ukkāsatanipātasamākulamiva), like kaṇikāra flowers (kaṇikārapupphamiva) scattered without interruption (nirantara), like powder (cuṇṇamiva) of Chinese flour (cīnapiṭṭha) thrown (khitta) by the force of the wind (vāyuvega), and like a forest clearing (vanaantaraṃ) shimmering and sparkling with dispersed and scattered rainbows (indadhanuvijjulatātārāgaṇappabhāvisaravipphuritaviccharitamiva ca) was (hoti).
And furthermore (ca pana), the body (sarīraṃ) of the Blessed One (bhagavato), adorned (anurañjitañca) with the eighty minor marks (asīti anubyañjana), was like a blossoming lotus (vikasitakamaluppalamiva), like a lake (saraṃ) full of blooming sabba water lilies (pāliphullamiva), a pāricchattakaṃ, like a sky sparkling with starlight (tārāmarīcivikasitamiva), like the surface of the sky (gaganatalaṃ) mocking with glory (siriyā avahasantamiva), and as for his garland (mālā) of thirty-two excellent marks (dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇa), shining with a fathom's extent of light (byāmappabhāparikkhepavilāsinī), having been strung together (ganthetvā), as if surpassing in glory (siriṃ siriyā abhibhavantimiva) the glory of thirty-two moon garlands (ṭhapitadvattiṃsacandamālāya), thirty-two sun garlands (dvattiṃsasūriyamālāya), [and] thirty-two emperor garlands (dvattiṃsacakkavattidvattiṃsasakkadevarājadvattiṃsamahābrahmānaṃ) placed in order (paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapita).
And those monks (bhikkhū) standing (ṭhitā) surrounding (parivāretvā) that Blessed One (tañca pana bhagavantaṃ) were all (sabbeva) of few wishes (appicchā), content (santuṭṭhā), fond of solitude (pavivittā), aloof (asaṃsaṭṭhā), exhorters (codakā), censors of evil (pāpagarahino), teachers (vattāro), tolerant of correction (vacanakkhamā), endowed with virtue (sīlasampannā), concentration (samādhi), wisdom (paññā), emancipation (vimutti), and the knowledge and vision of emancipation (vimuttiññāṇadassanasampannā).
In their midst (tesaṃ majjhe), the Blessed One (bhagavā), was like a golden pillar (kañcanathambho) surrounded (parikkhitto) by a red woolen rampart (rattakambalapākāra), like a golden boat (suvaṇṇanāvā) amidst a cluster of red lotus flowers (rattapadumasaṇḍamajjhagatā), like a tower of flame (aggikkhandho) encircled by a coral railing (pavāḷavedikāparikkhitto), or like the full moon (puṇṇacando) surrounded by the host of stars (tārāgaṇaparivārito), pleased (pīṇayati) the eyes (cakkhūni) even of the birds and beasts (migapakkhīnampi), much more (pageva) then [did he please] the eyes of gods and humans (devamanussānaṃ).
And on that day (tasmiñca pana divase), for the most part (yebhuyyena) eighty great theras (asītimahātherā) having made (karitvā) their cloud-colored (meghavaṇṇaṃ) rag robes (paṃsukūlaṃ) one-shouldered (ekaṃsaṃ), taking (ādāya) their walking sticks (kattaradaṇḍaṃ), like perfumed elephants (gandhahatthino) clad in solid armor (suvammavammitā viya), free from corruptions (vigatadosā), their corruptions ejected (vantadosā), their defilements shattered (bhinnakilesā), their tangles disentangled (vijaṭitajaṭā), and their bonds cut (chinnabandhanā) surrounded (parivārayiṃsu) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ).
He (so), himself (sayam) without lust (vītarāgo) [and] with those without lust (vītarāgehi), himself (sayam) without hatred (vītadoso) [and] with those without hatred (vītadosehi), himself (sayam) without delusion (vītamoho) [and] with those without delusion (vītamohehi), himself (sayam) without craving (vītataṇho) [and] with those without craving (vītataṇhehi), himself (sayam) without defilements (nikkileso) [and] with those without defilements (nikkilesehi), himself (sayam) awakened (buddho) [and] surrounded (parivārito) by those awakened after him (anubuddhehi); like filaments (kesaraṃ) surrounded by petals (pattaparivāritaṃ viya), like a seed pod (kaṇṇikā) surrounded by filaments (kesaraparivāritā viya), like a six-tusked elephant king (chaddanto nāgarājā) surrounded (parivārito viya) by eight thousand elephants (aṭṭhanāgasahassa), like a dhataraṭṭha swan king (haṃsarājā) surrounded (parivārito viya) by ninety thousand geese (navutihaṃsasahassa), like an emperor (cakkavattirājā) surrounded (parivārito viya) by an army (senaṅga), like Sakka (sakko) the king of the gods (devarājā) surrounded (parivārito viya) by a host of gods (devagaṇa), like Hārita (hārito) the Great Brahmā (mahābrahmā) surrounded (parivārito viya) by a host of Brahmās (brahmagaṇa), with the grace (līlāya) of a Buddha (buddha) produced (nibbattāya) through the power of merit (puññabala) accumulated (sañcita) for an immeasurable time (aparimitakāla), inconceivable (acinteyyāya), incomparable (anopamāya), like the moon (cando) across the sky (gaganatalaṃ), he was proceeding (paṭipanno hoti) on that road (taṃ maggaṃ).
Then (atha), thus (evaṃ) as the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) was going (gacchantaṃ) with the incomparable (anopamāya) grace of a Buddha (buddhalīlāya), and the monks (bhikkhū ca) with lowered eyes (okkhittacakkhū), tranquil senses (santindriye), and tranquil minds (santamānase) honoring (namassamāne) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃyeva) like the full moon (puṇṇacandaṃ viya) standing (ṭhitaṃ) in the upper sky (uparinabhe), having seen (disvāva), the wanderer (paribbājako) surveyed (avalokesi) his own assembly (attano parisaṃ).
She (sā hoti) was one whose burden (bhārabharitā) of various requisites (anekaparikkhāra) such as dilapidated stools (kājadaṇḍake), having hung (olambetvā), and having grasped (gahitā), ulugga, vilugga, piṭṭhaka, tidaṇḍa, peacock fans (morapiñcha), earthen bowls (mattikāpatta), sacks (pasibbaka), water pots (kuṇḍikādi).
"So-and-so's hands (hatthā) are beautiful (sobhaṇā), so-and-so's feet (pādā)," etc. [They were] those with loose tongues (mukharā) [filled with] meaningless words (evamādiniratthakavacanā) and scattered speech (vikiṇṇavācā), unsightly (adassanīyā), uninspiring (apāsādikā).
Having seen (disvā) that (taṃ), remorse (vippaṭisāro) arose (udapādi) in him (tassa).
Now (idāni) praise (vaṇṇo) of the Blessed One (bhagavato) should be spoken (vattabbo bhaveyya) by him (tena).
Since (yasmā) he (panesa) is constantly jealous (niccampi bhagavantaṃ usūyati) because of the loss (hāniyā) of gain (lābha) and honor (sakkāra) as well as the loss (hāniyā) of his following (pakkha).
For (hi) so long as (yāva) a Buddha (buddho) does not arise (nuppajjati) in the world (loke), just so long (tāva) do gain (lābha) and honor (sakkārā) arise (nibbattanti); but from the arising (buddhuppādato) of a Buddha (paṭṭhāya) there is diminished gain (parihīnalābha) and honor (sakkārā); like glow-worms (khajjopanakā) at sunrise (sūriyuggamane) they undergo (āpajjanti) a state of being without glory (nissirīkataṃ viya).
Moreover, at the time (santike) when Upatissa (upatissa) and Kolita (kolitānañca) went forth (pabbajitakāleyeva) under Sañjaya (sañjayassa), the wanderers (paribbājakā) had a great assembly (mahāparisā ahesuṃ); but when they (tesu) had departed (pakkantesu), that (sāpi) assembly (parisā) of theirs (tesaṃ) was split (bhinnā).
Thus (iti), because of these two (imehi dvīhi) reasons (kāraṇehi) why (yasmā) this wanderer (ayaṃ paribbājako) is constantly jealous (niccampi bhagavantaṃ usūyati), therefore (tasmā) vomiting up (uggiranto) that (taṃ) poison (visuggāraṃ) of jealousy (usūya), he speaks (bhāsatīti) only dispraise (avaṇṇameva) of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa); it should be understood (veditabbo).

2. Atha kho bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ rājāgārake ekarattivāsaṃ upagacchi upagañchi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Suppiyopi kho paribbājako ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ rājāgārake ekarattivāsaṃ upagacchi upagañchi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) antevāsinā brahmadattena māṇavena. Tatrapi sudaṃ suppiyo paribbājako anekapariyāyena buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; suppiyassa pana paribbājakassa antevāsī brahmadatto māṇavo anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Itiha te ubho ācariyantevāsī aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā viharanti.
2. Then the Blessed One, together with a community of monks ( bhikkhusaṅghena), approached and stayed for one night in the royal rest-house in Ambalaṭṭhika. Suppiya the Wanderer, together with his pupil Brahmadatta, the youth ( māṇavena), also approached and stayed for one night in the royal rest-house in Ambalaṭṭhika. And there, Suppiya the Wanderer, in many ways, spoke in dispraise ( avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati) of the Buddha, spoke in dispraise of the Dharma ( dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati), and spoke in dispraise of the Sangha ( saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati); but Brahmadatta, the pupil ( antevāsī) of Suppiya the Wanderer, in many ways, spoke in praise ( vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati) of the Buddha, spoke in praise of the Dharma, and spoke in praise of the Sangha. Thus, these two, teacher and pupil ( ācariyantevāsī), lived making assertions in direct contradiction to each other ( ujuvipaccanīkavādā viharanti).
2.Atha kho bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ rājāgārake ekarattivāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenāti bhagavā tāya buddhalīlāya gacchamāno anupubbena ambalaṭṭhikādvāraṃ pāpuṇitvā sūriyaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘akālo dāni gantuṃ, atthasamīpaṃ gato sūriyo’’ti ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ rājāgārake ekarattivāsaṃ upagacchi. Tattha ambalaṭṭhikāti rañño uyyānaṃ. Tassa kira dvārasamīpe taruṇaambarukkho atthi, taṃ ‘‘ambalaṭṭhikā’’ti vadanti. Tassa avidūre bhavattā uyyānampi ambalaṭṭhikā tveva saṅkhyaṃ gataṃ. Taṃ chāyūdakasampannaṃ pākāraparikkhittaṃ suyojitadvāraṃ mañjusā viya suguttaṃ. Tattha rañño kīḷanatthaṃ paṭibhānacittavicittaṃ agāraṃ akaṃsu. Taṃ ‘‘rājāgāraka’’nti vuccati. Suppiyopi khoti suppiyopi tasmiṃ ṭhāne sūriyaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘akālo dāni gantuṃ, bahū khuddakamahallakā paribbājakā, bahuparissayo ca ayaṃ maggo corehipi vāḷayakkhehipi vāḷamigehipi. Ayaṃ kho pana samaṇo gotamo uyyānaṃ paviṭṭho, samaṇassa ca gotamassa vasanaṭṭhāne devatā ārakkhaṃ gaṇhanti, handāhampi idha ekarattivāsaṃ upagantvā sveva gamissāmī’’ti tadevuyyānaṃ pāvisi. Tato bhikkhusaṅgho bhagavato vattaṃ dassetvā attano attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhesi. Paribbājakopi uyyānassa ekapasse paribbājakaparikkhāre otāretvā vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ attano parisāya. Pāḷiyamārūḷhavaseneva pana – ‘‘saddhiṃ attano antevāsinā brahmadattena māṇavenā’’ti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ vāsaṃ upagato pana so paribbājako rattibhāge dasabalaṃ olokesi. Tasmiñca samaye samantā vippakiṇṇatārakā viya padīpā jalanti, majjhe bhagavā nisinno hoti, bhikkhusaṅgho ca bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā. Tattha ekabhikkhussapi hatthakukkuccaṃ vā pādakukkuccaṃ vā ukkāsitasaddo vā khipitasaddo vā natthi. Sā hi parisā attano ca sikkhitasikkhatāya satthari ca gāravenāti dvīhi kāraṇehi nivāte padīpasikhā viya niccalā sannisinnāva ahosi. Paribbājako taṃ vibhūtiṃ disvā attano parisaṃ olokesi. Tattha keci hatthaṃ khipanti, keci pādaṃ, keci vippalapanti, keci nillālitajivhā paggharitakheḷā, dante khādantā kākacchamānā gharugharupassāsino sayanti. So ratanattayassa guṇavaṇṇe vattabbepi issāvasena puna avaṇṇameva ārabhi. Brahmadatto pana vuttanayeneva vaṇṇaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘tatrāpi sudaṃ suppiyo paribbājako’’ti sabbaṃ vattabbaṃ. Tattha tatrāpīti tasmimpi, ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ uyyāneti attho.
2. Then, indeed, the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, approached the royal rest house in Ambalaṭṭhikā for a one-night stay. The Blessed One, proceeding in that manner of a Buddha, gradually arrived at the gate of Ambalaṭṭhikā. Looking at the sun, he said, "It is not the right time to go, the sun has drawn near to its setting." And so the Blessed One approached the royal rest house in Ambalaṭṭhikā for a one-night stay.

There, "Ambalaṭṭhikā" means the king's garden.

It is said that near its gate, there is a young mango tree. They call it "Ambalaṭṭhikā."

Because it was not far from it, even the garden came to be known as Ambalaṭṭhikā.

It was complete with shade and water, surrounded by a wall, with well-arranged gates, and well-guarded like a box.

There, they had built a hall that was clever, varied in thought, and wondrous, for the king's amusement.

That is called "royal rest house (rājāgāraka)."

Suppiya also, having looked at the sun in that place, said, "It is not the right time to go, there are many small and old wanderers, and this road is full of dangers from thieves, wild yakṣas, and wild beasts.

This śramaṇa Gotama has entered the garden, and the deities guard the dwelling place of the śramaṇa Gotama, come, I too, having spent a night here, will go tomorrow.” So he entered that very garden.

Then the community of monks, having shown their duty to the Blessed One, each considered their own dwelling place.

The wanderer also, having unloaded the wanderer's equipment on one side of the garden, approached a dwelling, together with his assembly.

But in the language of the Pāli, it is said, "together with his pupil, the young man Brahmadatta (brahmadattena māṇavena)."

Having thus approached a dwelling, that wanderer, in the night, looked upon the Ten-Powered One.

And at that time, lamps were burning all around like scattered stars, and in the midst, the Blessed One was seated, with the community of monks surrounding the Blessed One.

There, not even one monk fidgeted with his hands, or fidgeted with his feet, or made any sound of coughing, or sound of clearing the throat.

That assembly, indeed, through their self-discipline and out of reverence for the Teacher, was as still and motionless as the flame of a lamp in a windless place.

The wanderer, having seen that splendor (vibhūtiṃ), looked upon his own assembly.

There, some were gesticulating with their hands, some with their feet, some were chattering, some with tongues lolling, drooling saliva, biting their teeth, wheezing, snorting, and sleeping.

He, although he should have spoken of the virtues and qualities of the Triple Gem (ratanattayassa guṇavaṇṇe), because of jealousy, instead, began to speak only of their faults (avaṇṇameva ārabhi).

Brahmadatta, however, spoke in praise, just as it was said.

Therefore it was said, "There also, it seems, Suppiya the wanderer" - all of that should be said.

There, "There also" means in that, in the garden in Ambalaṭṭhikā, this is the meaning.
3
3. Atha kho sambahulānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhitānaṃ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayaṃ saṅkhiyadhammo udapādi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso, yāvañcidaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikatā suppaṭividitā. Ayañhi suppiyo paribbājako anekapariyāyena buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; suppiyassa pana paribbājakassa antevāsī brahmadatto māṇavo anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Itihame ubho ācariyantevāsī aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti bhikkhusaṅghañcā’’ti.
3. Then, a number of monks, having risen in the early morning, gathered and sat in the Round Pavilion, and this train of thought arose among them: "Wonderful, friends! Marvelous, friends! How thoroughly the Blessed One (Bhagavatā), the Knower, the Seer, the Worthy One (Arhat), the perfectly enlightened Buddha (sammāsambuddhena), has understood the diversity in the inclinations of beings (sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikatā)!"

For this wanderer Suppiya (Suppiyo paribbājako) speaks in many ways in dispraise of the Buddha (buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati), the Dharma (dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati), and the Sangha (saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati); while the student of Suppiya (Suppiyassa pana paribbājakassa antevāsī), the youth Brahmadatta (Brahmadatto māṇavo), speaks in many ways in praise of the Buddha (buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati), the Dharma (dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati), and the Sangha (saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati).

And so, those two, teacher and pupil (ubhō ācariyantevāsī), making assertions directly opposed to each other (aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā), followed closely behind the Blessed One (Bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti) and the community of monks (bhikkhusaṅghañcā)"
3.Sambahulānanti bahukānaṃ. Tattha vinayapariyāyena tayo janā ‘‘sambahulā’’ti vuccanti. Tato paraṃ saṅgho. Suttantapariyāyena pana tayo tayova tato paṭṭhāya sambahulā. Idha suttantapariyāyena ‘‘sambahulā’’ti veditabbā. Maṇḍalamāḷeti katthaci dve kaṇṇikā gahetvā haṃsavaṭṭakacchannena katā kūṭāgārasālāpi ‘‘maṇḍalamāḷo’’ti vuccati, katthaci ekaṃ kaṇṇikaṃ gahetvā thambhapantiṃ parikkhipitvā katā upaṭṭhānasālāpi ‘‘maṇḍalamāḷo’’ti vuccati. Idha pana nisīdanasālā ‘‘maṇḍalamāḷo’’ti veditabbo. Sannisinnānanti nisajjanavasena. Sannipatitānanti samodhānavasena. Ayaṃ saṅkhiyadhammoti saṅkhiyā vuccati kathā , kathādhammoti attho. Udapādīti uppanno. Katamo pana soti? Acchariyaṃ āvusoti evamādi. Tattha andhassa pabbatārohaṇaṃ viya niccaṃ na hotīti acchariyaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva saddanayo. Ayaṃ pana aṭṭhakathānayo – accharāyogganti acchariyaṃ. Accharaṃ paharituṃ yuttanti attho. Abhūtapubbaṃ bhūtanti abbhutaṃ. Ubhayaṃ petaṃ vimhayassevādhivacanaṃ. Yāvañcidanti yāva ca idaṃ tena suppaṭividitatāya appameyyattaṃ dasseti. Tena bhagavatā jānatā…pe… suppaṭividitāti etthāyaṃ saṅkhepattho.
